rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row closes at Eccl.2.19 on the strength of the hated-life anaphora without disclosing that the tachat-hashemesh refrain running through 2.17-2.19 continues unbroken past the row's own seam into 2.20 and 2.22. OL (same core defect, plus a second): the refrain's own only consecutive multi-verse run book-wide crosses this exact seam undisclosed, and a distinct heir/labor thread (adam-labor collocation opened at 2:18) is independently resumed at 2:21, also undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Byte-tier re-derivation confirms the core defect both primaries name is real and their framing is accurate. tachat-hashemesh (skeleton tier: תחת השמש tokens) is present at MT 2:17, 2:18, 2:19, 2:20 and 2:22 but ABSENT at 2:21 and 2:23 (re-swept against consonantal_index.json, all 222 verses): the formula stands in exactly 27 verses book-wide, and MT 2:17-2:20 is its ONLY four-verse consecutive run in the whole book (every other hit is an isolated single verse) -- independently re-confirmed by a fresh full-book skeleton sweep, matching OL's digit exactly. This is a tier-1 frame-spine device (book_strategy Eccl SS2c) straddling the row's own 2.19|2.20 closing seam, which the standing CROSS-SEAM COHESION rule treats as arguing continuity against the row unless disclosed. The row's own observed_substrate_signals already tags 'under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh' for this row -- so the device is KNOWN to the writer -- yet device_notes addresses only the internal 2:17/2:18 hated-root pairing (הֶ֖בֶל ... אֶת כָּל עֲמָלִ֔י) and never weighs the refrain's continuation as counter-evidence. OL's second, independent finding also re-derives clean: 2:18 closes שֶׁ֣אַנִּיחֶ֔נּוּ לָאָדָ֖ם שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽי ('...to the man who will be after me') and 2:21 opens the parallel וּלְאָדָ֞ם שֶׁלֹּ֤א עָֽמַל בּוֹ֙ ('...and to a man who has not labored in it') -- the same heir/labor collocation (adam + amal) resumed two verses past the boundary, undisclosed on either side. LF and OL are adjudicated as the SAME core defect (undisclosed cross-seam tachat-hashemesh) with OL additionally and correctly identifying a second, distinct undisclosed cross-seam device (heir/labor) that strengthens rather than replaces LF's finding.
rulings.remedy: Add one disclosure sentence to device_notes naming both cross-seam continuations: (1) the tachat-hashemesh refrain continues into 2:20 and 2:22, and MT 2:17-2:20 is the refrain's own sole four-verse consecutive run book-wide (sweep: 27 verses, 1 run of length 4 at MT 2:17-2:20, skeleton tier); (2) the heir/labor thread opened at 2:18's closing clause is resumed at 2:21's parallel construction. Per the standing rule this is disclosure only -- the savoti restart-verb driver at 2:20 remains a legitimate boundary signal on its own bytes; the cross-seam devices do not by themselves overturn the split. Test the cure must pass: a fresh cross-seam sweep against both device families over MT 2:17-2:23 finds every hit named in device_notes, not just tagged in observed_substrate_signals.

rulings.challenge_claim: observed_substrate_signals declares 'frame_seams.shavti_turns', a signal byte-absent from the row's own span and repudiated by the row's own rejected_alternative prose; the two in-span tachat-hashemesh instances go undeclared, and the savoti spelling's second book site (MT 7:25) is withheld from the 'distinct formula' warrant.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived clean. The quoted opener וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.20, byte tier) is verse-initial and correctly identified as the savav root. A fresh skeleton sweep confirms shavti (root shuv: וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי / וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי / שַׁ֜בְתִּי) stands ONLY at MT 4:1, 4:7 and 9:11 -- zero hits in 2:20-2:23 -- so the declared signal 'frame_seams.shavti_turns' has no byte support inside this row's span, exactly as OL states; the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative explicitly argues savav and shuv must not be blended, which makes the observed_substrate_signals tag self-contradicting (a driver-dependent-field defect per the standing rule). The span DOES carry tachat-hashemesh at 2:20 and 2:22 (וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֖י לְיַאֵ֣שׁ אֶת לִבִּ֑י עַ֚ל כָּל הֶ֣עָמָ֔ל שֶׁעָמַ֖לְתִּי תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ ... כִּ֠י מֶֽה הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽאָדָם֙ בְּכָל עֲמָל֔וֹ וּבְרַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑ו שֶׁה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ) -- 2 of the 27-verse inventory -- undeclared in observed_substrate_signals. The savoti spelling re-sweep confirms exactly 2 book sites, MT 2:20 and 7:25 (סַבּ֨וֹתִֽי opens 7:25), so the 'distinct turning-formula' warrant is sound as distinctness-from-shavti but overstates uniqueness; OL's framing and severity are both accurate.
rulings.remedy: Remove 'frame_seams.shavti_turns' from observed_substrate_signals (byte-absent from the span) and replace with an accurate tag naming the row's own savav-root turn, if the controlled vocabulary carries one, else state the omission explicitly; add 'under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh' for the 2 in-span instances (2:20, 2:22); in device_notes disclose that the savoti spelling recurs once more at MT 7:25 (sweep: 2 verses total) rather than implying a one-site formula. Test the cure must pass: every observed_substrate_signals tag has at least one byte-confirmed instance inside the row's own verse span.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's closing warrant at 2:26 is carried entirely in WEB English with no Hebrew splice, and strongest_rejected_alternative misdescribes MT 3:1 as an instance of the et-plus-infinitive list template when the bytes place that template at 3:2-8, with 3:1 itself a superscription.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived clean on both counts. boundary_evidence_refs cites oshb:Eccl.2.24 but no oshb: ref for 2:26 -- the row's actual closing quote ('This also is vanity and a chasing after wind', web:Eccl.2.26) ships with no pointed splice; the underlying bytes are הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, 1 of the 7-verse reut-ruach inventory and 1 of the 30 hevel-family verses, confirming the content is boundary-relevant and therefore subject to the mandatory-splice engagement rule. MT 3:1 itself reads לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם -- its single et governs a prepositional phrase (tachat hashamayim), there is no infinitive in the verse, and it carries the book's sole zman-noun occurrence (re-swept: 1 verse). The et-plus-infinitive template proper begins at 3:2, opening עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת. MT 3:1 is a superscription, not a template instance; the boundary itself survives on that superscription reading, but the rejected_alternative's description of 3:1 as the template is byte-false.
rulings.remedy: Splice הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.26, byte tier) into boundary_rationale/boundary_evidence_refs alongside the existing WEB quote. Rewrite the 3:1 clause in strongest_rejected_alternative from '3:1 opens... the fixed et-clause list template' to describe 3:1 as the catalogue's superscription (single et governing a prepositional phrase, no infinitive, sole zman-noun in the book) preceding the et-plus-infinitive series that actually opens at 3:2. Test the cure must pass: every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carries a pointed splice and tier label; every grammatical description of a cited verse matches its own morphology, re-checked word by word.

rulings.challenge_claim: The setumah cited as the catalogue's OPENING bracket at MT 3:1 actually TERMINATES 3:1 (argues a 3:1|3:2-8 division the row denies), and the 'every line follows the et-plus-infinitive template' universal is refuted by the row's own closing quote (3:8) and by 3:1 itself.
rulings.grounds: Both sub-claims re-derived clean from the raw WLC source (the canonical OSHB Eccl.xml underlying pmarks_Eccl.json, read read-only as the same staged source build_pmarks.py consumes -- not a forbidden-lane file). Direct inspection of the verse element structure shows <seg type="x-samekh"> for MT 3:1 placed AFTER 3:1's own x-sof-pasuq seg, still INSIDE the Eccl.3.1 verse element, before the Eccl.3.2 verse opens -- structurally identical to the PE seg at MT 1:11 (also after 1:11's own sof-pasuq, inside the 1:11 element), which the book strategy agrees terminates/closes the prologue poem. By the same structural logic the 3:1 samekh terminates MT 3:1, dividing it from 3:2 -- an INTERNAL division inside the row's own span, not an opening bracket for the row. The MT 3:8 samekh is structurally the same shape (after 3:8's own sof-pasuq) and correctly closes the catalogue at the 3:8|3:9 edge, as the row states. So the row's 'bracket opening the catalogue' label for 3:1 is directionally backward; its only intra-span Masoretic paragraph signal in fact argues a 3:1|3:2-8 split. Second sub-claim: a fresh per-verse retally of all 29 et-tokens in MT 3:1-3:8 finds 26 governing an infinitive construct across 3:2-3:7 and the first pair of 3:8 (עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א), while the second pair of 3:8 closes on bare nouns, עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם ('a time of war and a time of peace'), and 3:1's own et governs the prepositional phrase in לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם -- 3 of 29 slots are non-infinitival, 2 of them inside the row's own quoted closing verse. 'Every line follows the et-plus-infinitive template' is byte-false and ships with no digit-bearing qualifier, violating the standing universal-claim rule. Both defects are independently confirmed, hard, and sit in the row's core rationale/evidence citations -- OL's high severity is appropriate. Note for the record: neither defect threatens the actual chunking decision, since the owner ruling (SS6) locks list_catalogue 3:1-8 as one row on FUNCTION grounds and parashah marks are TIER-3, NEVER a boundary driver -- the fix is corrective disclosure and a rewritten universal, not a re-boundary.
rulings.remedy: (1) Correct the boundary_evidence_refs annotation for oshb:Eccl.3.1: remove '(setumah, single-witness, tier-3 bracket opening the catalogue)' and replace with a direction-accurate note -- the samekh terminates MT 3:1 (same shape as the MT 1:11 PE), marking an internal division preceding the 3:2-8 paired-clause series, disclosed as tier-3 single-witness and NEVER a boundary driver; the unity of 3:1-8 rests on the owner's function ruling, not this mark. (2) Rewrite the universal in boundary_rationale to a digit-qualified claim: 26 of the poem's 29 et-slots govern an infinitive; 3:8's second pair and 3:1's own et govern nouns/a prepositional phrase, not infinitives (re-tally: 26/29 infinitival, byte tier). Test the cure must pass: every cited Masoretic mark's direction is checked against its raw seg placement (before vs. after the verse's own sof-pasuq) before being labeled opening or closing; no unqualified universal survives a full re-tally of its own governing construction.

rulings.grounds: Re-derived clean. Second: a fresh contiguous-skeleton sweep for the mah-yitron opener returns exactly 3 sites book-wide -- MT 1:3, MT 3:9, and oshb:Eccl.5.15 = web:Eccl.5.16 (וּמַה יִּתְר֣וֹן ל֔וֹ, dual-cited per the offset-zone rule) -- not the 2-site link to 1:3 alone the row's rejected_alternative implies; the bare profit-noun (yitron) stands in 9 verses, independently re-confirmed. OL's framing and medium severity are both accurate: this is a field-accuracy and comparative-claim defect, not a boundary error -- the row's own close at 3:11 (בְעִתּ֑וֹ region) before the yadati restart at 3:12 is unaffected.
rulings.remedy: Remove 'under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh' from observed_substrate_signals (byte-absent from 3:9-3:11) or replace it with the device the span actually carries (the mah-yitron/profit-noun echo alone). Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to drop the false 'tachat-hashemesh-adjacent register' comparison and to disclose the mah-yitron opener as a 3-site formula (MT 1:3, 3:9, oshb:Eccl.5.15 = web:Eccl.5.16) rather than implying a 2-site link. rulings.grounds: LF and OL are adjudicated as raising DISTINCT defects on the same row, both byte-confirmed. LF's defect: MT 3:9 opens with מַה יִּתְרוֹן֙ (the mah-yitron question, no perception-verb root), and the perception verb רָאִ֣יתִי occurs first at MT 3:10, the neighboring row's SECOND verse -- yet this row's strongest_rejected_alternative characterizes 'the row before it' as opening with the 'I saw' burden-observation. Byte-false as stated; LF's low severity is apt since it misdescribes a NEIGHBOR, not this row's own span. OL's defect: boundary_evidence_refs for this row cites only oshb:Eccl.3.13 (mid-verse, a supporting clause, שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה), never the boundary driver itself; boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative both name the driver only as bare transliteration 'yadati' with no pointed splice or tier, violating the mandatory Hebrew-engagement rule for boundary-relevant claims. A fresh sweep for the verb confirms it is a real and unusually tight internal bracket had it been spliced: יָדַ֕עְתִּי (MT 3:12) and יָדַ֗עְתִּי (MT 3:14) are 2 of only 4 book-wide sites (MT 1:17, 2:14, 3:12, 3:14) and the ONLY 2 that are verse-initial -- both inside this row. rulings.remedy: (1) OL's defect: splice יָדַ֕עְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.3.12, byte tier) and יָדַ֗עְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.3.14, byte tier) into boundary_rationale/strongest_rejected_alternative in place of the bare transliteration 'yadati'; remove 'sentence_zone_texture.catchword_adjacency' from observed_substrate_signals since the span is not in either sentence zone. (2) LF's defect: correct strongest_rejected_alternative's description of the neighboring row -- replace 'the I saw burden-observation that opens the row before it' with an accurate description (3:9, that row's own opening verse, is the mah-yitron question; the perception verb first occurs at 3:10). Test the cure must pass: every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carries a pointed splice and tier; every cross-row characterization of a neighbor's opening verse is checked against that neighbor's own first word; every observed_substrate_signals tag matches the row's actual parent/zone location.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row asserts a chain 'with no internal restart marker' while its own first verse opens with a subordinator binding it to 3:18, the animal catchword straddles that seam undisclosed on this side, 3:21 opens with a formula the same cluster treats as a boundary signal elsewhere, and the in-span hevel refrain instance is undeclared.
rulings.grounds: All four sub-claims re-derived clean. (1) MT 3:19 opens כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי -- a causal subordinator (ki) whose clause depends on 3:18 -- not an independent restart; the row's own 'no internal restart marker' framing does not address this dependency. (2) The animal catchword (behemah) stands at MT 3:18 (בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם), 3:19, and 3:21 -- 3 verses -- straddling this row's own OPENING seam (3:18|3:19); the neighboring row (P01-015) discloses the forward continuation into this row, but this row discloses nothing on the backward side, an asymmetric cross-seam gap. (3) MT 3:21 opens with the who-knows formula מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ, one of exactly 4 book sites (MT 2:19, 3:21, 6:12, 8:1) -- and this SAME cluster's own P01-009 closes ON the MT 2:19 instance of that formula (וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ...) as its row-closing heir-uncertainty verdict; treating the identical formula as verdict-bearing at 2:19 and as 'no marker at all' at 3:21 within the same cluster is an internal inconsistency the row does not address (this does not by itself relocate the 3:21|3:22 boundary, which rests independently on the raiti restart at 3:22). (4) MT 3:19 closes on כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל -- a hakol-hevel instance (1 of 6 hakol-hevel verses, 1 of the 30 hevel-family verses, both independently re-confirmed) -- inside the row's own span, yet observed_substrate_signals lists only 'elohim_yhwh.yhwh_absence', leaving the book's central refrain undeclared where it actually occurs. None of the four defects overturns the row's own boundary (3:19-21 as one unit before the 3:22 raiti restart remains defensible on its own bytes); OL's medium severity is apt for a rationale/disclosure-quality defect of this breadth.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite 'no internal restart marker' to acknowledge that 3:19 opens with a causal subordinate clause (כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי...) dependent on 3:18, and to address rather than silently deny the who-knows formula at 3:21, noting its consistent treatment (or explicit distinguishing argument) relative to the 2:19 instance elsewhere in this same cluster. Disclose the animal catchword crossing this row's own opening seam (mirroring the forward disclosure the neighboring row already gives). Add the hakol-hevel token at MT 3:19 to observed_substrate_signals. Test the cure must pass: no 'no marker' claim ships without checking the verse-initial word of every verse in the span against the book's own catalogued formula inventory; every refrain instance inside the row's own span is disclosed, not only the divine-name absence.
